topLine: The Minns government reversed its new single-use plastics rule for dine-in coffee, with cafes again able to serve takeaway cups to customers drinking in; the environment minister said the issue needed clearing up. Planning and housing dominated elsewhere, with the government signalling stalled but "significant" projects will not be killed off by a 12-month construction deadline, while the Herald's commentary pages weighed Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane's Long Bay jail proposal and the risk One Nation poses to Labor. In the Illawarra, the Mercury reports local Labor MPs Paul Scully and Ryan Park have declined to back union calls for the University of Wollongong's governing council to quit after an ICAC matter.

In the Illawarra, the Mercury reports local Labor MPs Paul Scully and Ryan Park have declined to back union calls for the University of Wollongong's governing council to quit after an ICAC matter.
briefing.localWatch: Shoalhaven City Council has adopted a new youth engagement model to gather young residents' priorities, and Transport for NSW is raising the speed limit on the Figtree M1 Princes Motorway on-ramp, the main northern road corridor out of the region. Illawarra Labor MPs are also under pressure over the University of Wollongong's governing body.

stories.headline: Council backs new way to connect with young people
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council says it will set up a new youth engagement model to improve how it communicates with young people and to identify their priorities for the Shoalhaven.

stories.headline: The 'simple' changes set to relieve M1 Motorway congestion at busy on-ramp
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Transport for NSW is lifting the speed limit on the Figtree on-ramp to the M1 Princes Motorway to 100km/h, with new line markings, in a bid to ease congestion for commuters.

stories.headline: Hanson sidesteps questions on cartoon controversies
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports One Nation leader Pauline Hanson avoided questions about the party's Bluey-style cartoons, which have been criticised by other politicians, and about a colouring book that has also attracted criticism.

stories.headline: NSW government backflips on brand-new coffee cup law
stories.summary: The NSW government has reversed part of its new plastics laws, so cafes can continue serving dine-in customers in disposable cups. The Guardian reports the requirement for venues to offer mugs to people drinking in will be scrapped, quoting the environment minister saying "we need to clear this up". The Premier told reporters he uses disposable cups himself.

stories.headline: Housing developments get reprieve as soaring costs hamper building
stories.summary: The Australian Financial Review reports the NSW government will let stalled housing projects it considers significant proceed even where they have missed a 12-month deadline to start construction, as building costs rise.

stories.headline: ‘System is beyond broken’: David has been stuck in a Sydney hospital for almost four months
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports more than 1000 patients across NSW are "stranded" in hospital — medically ready for discharge but unable to leave because no aged care place is available. One patient, David Witt, has been in a Sydney hospital for close to four months.

stories.headline: Minns Labor Government fast tracks road safety upgrades at nine regional locations
stories.summary: The government says targeted road safety improvements will be delivered at nine regional NSW locations following recent fatal crashes, describing the work as a quick response to identified safety risks.

stories.headline: ‘No-brainer’: Parramatta Road light rail plan to unlock 100k homes
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports on a proposed Parramatta Road light rail line, which backers say could unlock about 100,000 homes.

stories.headline: Menindee Lakes water levels drop to lowest in five years as experts warn of mass fish deaths
stories.summary: The Guardian reports the NSW government has imposed upstream water use restrictions after combined storage at the Menindee Lakes in western NSW fell below 480 gigalitres this month, the first time since 2021. Experts quoted by the paper warn of possible mass fish deaths over summer.

stories.headline: NRMA Insurance's $12m blunder as drivers overcharged for green slip costs
stories.summary: The ABC reports thousands of NSW motorists were overcharged for compulsory third party green slips after NRMA Insurance applied incorrect risk ratings based on where vehicles were garaged. The report says the State Insurance Regulatory Authority has fined the insurer.

stories.headline: Women at NSW correctional facility left without access to period products
stories.summary: The ABC reports an inspection of a 24-hour holding facility for prisoners in NSW found menstruating women were left for days without sanitary supplies.

stories.headline: Construction underway on major upgrade to Thornton Public School
stories.summary: The government says work has started on a multimillion-dollar upgrade of Thornton Public School in the Hunter that will almost double its permanent classrooms.

stories.headline: Why Illawarra Labor MPs won't join calls for university council to step down at UOW
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Labor MPs Paul Scully and Ryan Park have taken a position at odds with union calls for the University of Wollongong's governing council to resign following an ICAC matter.

stories.headline: Outback pools to open unsupervised after struggling to find lifeguards
stories.summary: The ABC reports one remote NSW council plans to allow unsupervised access to all its public pools after struggling to recruit lifeguards, a move the report says some consider a safety concern, while a shortage of lifeguards threatens closures elsewhere.

stories.headline: Chris Minns is right to fear a One Nation wipeout
stories.summary: The Herald argues the Premier has reason to worry about One Nation, suggesting some Labor voters are unimpressed with Macquarie Street and asking whether Pauline Hanson's party and other contrarians can convert that discontent. The piece is opinion.

stories.headline: Opposition’s Long Bay idea not the negative gear portrayed by Labor
stories.summary: The Herald argues that Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane's proposal to sell Long Bay jail to help ease the state's housing crisis has merit, and that Labor's characterisation of it is unfair. This is the writer's view, not a reported finding.

stories.headline: The federal Labor brand has lost its star power
stories.summary: The AFR argues the Prime Minister can afford to wait for global inflation pressures to ease, but that Labor state premiers facing elections in the near term do not have that time. Relevant background for NSW as 2027 approaches.

stories.headline: Guardian Essential poll: One Nation and Labor’s primary vote on par as discontent with Albanese rises
stories.summary: The Guardian reports its Essential poll has One Nation's primary vote level with Labor's, and the Prime Minister's disapproval rating at 56 per cent — the equal highest recorded in Essential polling since he took the role in 2022.

stories.headline: Albanese trips over the truth when it suits. If he’s not careful, it could be contagious
stories.summary: A Herald opinion piece criticises the Prime Minister's handling of questions about a $6 million grant to the Marrickville Golf Club, describing the episode as a needless entanglement. It is the writer's opinion.

stories.headline: Snub or snafu? Chris Minns almost failed to fly at Western Sydney International
stories.summary: The Herald's CBD column reports the Premier, originally slated to speak after the Prime Minister at Western Sydney International, had to step in after the master of ceremonies overlooked him.
